turns.en: But the fundamentals really continue to be tight. Now, the question is, was this now correctly priced in? Or are we going to see that oil and a lot of these refined products will continue to actually head higher?
turns.zh: 但基本面确实依然紧张。问题是，这现在是否已被正确计入价格？还是我们会看到原油以及很多成品油实际上会继续走高？

turns.en: And this is the big story because right now, higher crude and higher diesel and all these other prices are what is actually driving the inflation expectations, which has been the stress point in the credit markets.
turns.zh: 这才是大故事，因为眼下，更高的原油、更高的柴油以及所有其他价格，才是真正在推高通胀预期的东西，而这一直是信贷市场的压力点。

turns.en: And so really the path of oil here is going to decide a lot as to whether or not things like CTA triggers on the S&P are vulnerable. One thing we have here is oils currently had a very overbought condition and absorbing and consolidating in a trade range.
turns.zh: 所以原油接下来的路径，将在很大程度上决定诸如标普上的 CTA 触发点是否脆弱。我们这里的一个情况是，原油目前处于非常超买的状况，正在一个交易区间里消化、盘整。

turns.en: As we get into the weeks ahead, we'll really find out whether this is a stable level of oil or whether another leg higher gets started at this moment.
turns.zh: 随着我们进入接下来几周，我们会真正弄清：这是原油的一个稳定水平，还是此刻又要启动另一段上行。

turns.en: I want to respect the prevailing trend because this moment, a lot of the geopolitical macro drivers have not been resolved. And so expecting somehow that there's going to be a deep reversion isn't supported by this.
turns.zh: 我想尊重当前的趋势，因为此刻很多地缘政治的宏观驱动因素都还没有解决。所以，指望会出现某种深度的均值回归，这一点并不被现实支持。

turns.en: I am certainly there could be a surprise resolution to the Middle Eastern conflict, but at least as of this moment, that doesn't seem to be an immediate reality.
turns.zh: 当然，中东冲突有可能出现意想不到的化解，但至少截至此刻，那似乎还不是一个马上会实现的现实。

turns.en: Yeah, and Patrick, when we look at that dollar, I mean, it produced a decisive upside reversal following that Fed decision yesterday. Now we reclaim the psychologically important level of $100 on the DXY.
turns.zh: 是的，Patrick，当我们看美元时，我是说，在昨天那个美联储决定之后，它出现了一轮决定性的向上反转。现在我们重新站上了 DXY 那个心理重要的 100 关口。

turns.en: Now, does this mark the resumption of the dollar bull trend? Or could it simply be a short-term reaction to that Fed's caucus message? The most interesting thing that came from the Fed was that a lot of different assets within the intermarket actually held firm.
turns.zh: 那么，这标志着美元牛市趋势的重启吗？还是它可能只是对美联储那个鹰派信息的短期反应？——来自美联储最有意思的一点是，跨市场（intermarket）里很多不同的资产其实都稳住了。

turns.en: In other words, they were, well, let's call it right priced for the expectation of what was going to happen. The one area where we saw a material repricing was the dollar.
turns.zh: 换句话说，它们——好吧，我们就说——针对将会发生什么的预期，定价是正确的。我们唯一看到实质性重新定价的领域，就是美元。

turns.en: And the dollar bullishly broke out on the DXY. And it was very much driven by a breakdown in the euro. And that happened in that response. To me, obviously, the Fed is the catalyst for this sharp reversal.
turns.zh: 美元在 DXY 上看涨突破。这在很大程度上是由欧元的跌破驱动的，而那是在这一反应中发生的。对我来说，显然美联储是这轮急转的催化剂。

turns.en: But now we're coming to some interesting technical observations, which is the US dollar did not make a low or low at any point. The breakdown in the dollar was driven when Bascent started to intervene in the long bond, but with the hawkishness of the Fed, clearly the narrative is shifting back.
turns.zh: 但现在我们要谈到一些有意思的技术观察：美元在任何时点都没有创出更低的低点。此前美元的跌破，是在 Besant 开始干预长债时被触发的，但随着美联储转鹰，显然叙事正在转回来。

turns.en: The question is, is this breakout for real? One day it doesn't make a new trend. And certainly there isn't enough follow-through yet to confirm that somehow the US dollar is in a new bull trend.
turns.zh: 问题是，这次突破是真的吗？一天的行情并不构成一个新趋势。而且显然还没有足够的后续跟进，来确认美元已经进入了新的牛市趋势。

turns.en: But this is probably the single most interesting thing to watch in the post FOMC market reactions, because there's all sorts of implications to another resumption of a US dollar bull advance.
turns.zh: 但这可能是 FOMC 之后市场反应里最值得关注的单单一件事，因为美元的又一轮牛市升势重启，会带来各种各样的影响。

turns.en: That's certainly not guaranteed at this moment. But if that became the unfolding reality, there's all sorts of implications on different asset prices that were anticipating a weak dollar environment.
turns.zh: 这在当下当然还没有保证。但如果那成为逐步展开的现实，那么对各种原本预期弱美元环境的资产价格，都会有种种影响。

turns.en: Yeah, now let's talk about gold, because I feel like it's getting pulled in every direction and the price lately has been pretty quiet. And what's interesting is that in the caught report, we're still seeing considerable long exposure being rebuilt.
turns.zh: 是的，现在我们聊聊黄金，因为我觉得它正被往各个方向拉扯，而最近价格相当平静。有意思的是，在持仓报告（COT report）里，我们仍看到相当多的多头敞口在被重建。

turns.en: But this move in the dollar and the yields, you know, could definitely provide more headwind for the precious metal. But how do you view this pullback?
turns.zh: 但美元和收益率的这一动向，你知道，绝对可能给贵金属带来更多逆风。那你怎么看这轮回调？

turns.en: Well, this is exactly what I was talking about with this dollar breakout. And gold is the perfect example of that. When you go back and look at what drove the correction in gold over the last six months, it was rising real rates and a US dollar that was generally strong.
turns.zh: 嗯，这正是我说美元突破时所讲的。黄金就是一个完美的例子。当你回头看过去六个月是什么驱动了黄金的回调，那是上升的实际利率（real rates）和一个总体走强的美元。

turns.en: Now, when we saw a month ago or more, was the US dollar started to weaken and real rates were a little bit stable. And it really looked like this could be the point where we had the macro backdrop for a potential gold and Bitcoin breakout.
turns.zh: 而我们在一个多月前看到的，是美元开始走弱、实际利率略趋稳定。看起来这真的可能就是那个点：我们拥有了黄金和比特币潜在突破所需的宏观背景。

turns.en: And they obviously did break out. But what we've seen since then is those perceived tailwinds were not really tailwinds. And maybe now may actually be headwinds.
turns.zh: 它们显然确实突破了。但自那之后我们看到的是，那些被认为的顺风其实并不是顺风，也许现在反而成了逆风。

turns.en: And so the big puzzle to solve here on gold was that was this a real breakout that we saw over the last month? And is this consolidation going to be bought on dip?
turns.zh: 所以黄金这里要解决的大难题是：过去一个月我们看到的，是一次真正的突破吗？而这次盘整，会不会被逢低买入（buy on dip）？

turns.en: Or have we just seen that the macro and the intermarket relationships may have pushed the gold breakout out forward into the fourth quarter and that we're going to see a far more range bound precious metal?
turns.zh: 还是说，我们只是看到宏观和跨市场的关系，可能把黄金的突破往后推到了第四季度，而我们将看到一个更加区间震荡的贵金属？

turns.en: For me, that line in the sand is right here right now as gold is testing this 4400 level. This is where we're going to find out whether or not this retracement is bought.
turns.zh: 对我来说，那条“分界线”就在此刻这里，因为黄金正在测试 4400 这个水平。这就是我们将要弄清、这轮回撤会不会被买入的地方。

turns.en: I want to see a reclaim of this 50 day moving average, a breakout of this declining wedge and a resumption of the bull trend. If we see any legitimate breakdowns to like 4200 or 4,000, it really does mean that this was a false start and it doesn't make it bearish for gold.
turns.zh: 我想看到它重新站上这条 50 日均线、突破这个下行楔形，并重启牛市趋势。如果我们看到任何真正的跌破，比如跌到 4200 或 4000，那确实意味着这是一次假启动，但这并不使黄金转为看跌。

turns.en: It just means that the gold bull market didn't start in this window and that it would be a story that would be starting later in the fourth quarter.
turns.zh: 它只是意味着，黄金牛市没有在这个窗口启动，而它会是一个将在第四季度晚些时候才开始的故事。

turns.en: Once we've finished this hiking cycle. All right, now I want to turn the copper because we have the most interesting positioning conflict in the asset.
turns.zh: 等我们结束这轮加息周期之后。好，现在我想转向铜，因为在这个资产上，我们有一个最有意思的持仓矛盾。

turns.en: Now, when looking at the big picture, the long term supply store remains extremely bullish, but large spec positioning has now reached the score of 100 over all look back periods.
turns.zh: 从大局看，长期供应的故事依然极度看涨，但大型投机持仓现在已经达到了在所有回看周期上均为 100 分的水平。

turns.en: Now, typically in general, how do you distinguish a fundamentally justified position in the long term from a dangerously crowded trade in the short to medium term?
turns.zh: 那么，一般而言，你如何区分一个在长期上由基本面支撑的合理持仓，与一个在中短期上危险拥挤的交易？

turns.en: So, Michelle, this is the puzzle to solve, right? We do have mine supply constraints, grid electrification, AI demand. All the structural bull cases are there to back this up, but this is consensus and everyone is fully positioned in this.
turns.zh: 所以，Michelle，这就是要解决的难题，对吧？我们确实有矿山供应约束、电网电气化、AI 需求。所有结构性的看涨理由都在那里支撑着它，但这已经是共识，每个人都已充分布局其中。

turns.en: And we are now at literally five year extremes in terms of long positioning, which is everyone's already in the story. Now, what we saw was some volatility here on the short term driven by concerns about how the tariffs were going to progress that spurred a 8% correction in copper in just a few days.
turns.zh: 而且我们在多头持仓上，现在真的处于五年极值，也就是说每个人都已经在这个故事里了。我们看到的是，短期内出现了一些波动，源于对关税将如何推进的担忧，这促使铜在短短几天里回调了 8%。

turns.en: Now, what's interesting here is this morning, we are getting the bounce and it's reclaiming that 50 day moving average. But to me, this is a make it or break it moment.
turns.zh: 有意思的是，今天早盘我们正在迎来反弹，它正重新站上那条 50 日均线。但对我来说，这是一个成败在此一举的时刻。

turns.en: This correction stalled right at the 50% retracement of that summer rally. And if the bulls can brush this off, reclaim, you know, 675 on the upside, there is room for the bulls to still maintain the strong trend and keep plugging on the upside.
turns.zh: 这轮回调恰好止步于那波夏季涨势的 50% 回撤位。如果多头能把这个甩开、重新站上上方的 675，那么多头仍有空间维持强势、继续在上方推进。

turns.en: But if we see that each rally starts getting distributed and then we start tripping up at the lows that we put in just earlier this week, then that becomes problematic because the trade is incredibly crowded.
turns.zh: 但如果我们看到每一次反弹都开始被派发，然后我们又在本周早些时候创下的低点处绊倒，那就会变得麻烦，因为这个交易拥挤得不得了。

turns.en: It'd be interesting to see if any of those weak hand longs can get shaken out with some downside volatility. At this moment, let's give the bulls a benefit of doubt, but again, very crowded and the volatility has really come back in.
turns.zh: 值得关注的是，看看那些“弱手”多头会不会被一些下行的波动甩出去。此刻，我们姑且对多头给予一点信任，但再说一次，非常拥挤，而且波动率确实又回来了。

turns.en: It'd be very interesting to see whether any traders get washed out. All right. Thank you for that, Patrick. Now, let's turn to this week's positioning pause.
turns.zh: 看看有没有交易者被洗出去，会非常有意思。好，谢谢你，Patrick。现在，我们转向本周的“持仓聚焦”。

turns.en: And that's where we talk about the clearest extreme outside the core markets we always cover. And this week, I want to talk about natural gas because when you look at the COT report and you look at that large speculator positioning, we fall into a score of zero across all look back periods.
turns.zh: 在这个环节，我们谈那些在我们常年覆盖的核心市场之外、最明显的极端情况。本周我想谈谈天然气，因为当你看 COT 报告、看大型投机者持仓时，我们在所有回看周期上都落到了 0 分。

turns.en: The one year, the three year, the five year now speculators are showing a net short positioning totaling about 220,000 contracts. Just to put that into simple terms, that's the lowest net positioning we've seen the last five years.
turns.zh: 一年、三年、五年——如今投机者显示出合计约 220,000 手合约的净空头持仓。用简单的话说，这是我们过去五年见到的最低净持仓水平。

turns.en: Now, do you think this extreme positioning creates that condition for major market squeeze or traders simply positioned correctly considering the fundamental backdrop?
turns.zh: 那么，你觉得这种极端持仓创造了发生重大市场挤压（squeeze）的条件，还是说考虑到基本面背景，交易者只是布局正确？

turns.en: Well, I actually think both in a sense that the traders are positioned correctly for the fundamentals. There's strong production inventory builds, a weather driven reduction in power demand, all of the things that would weaken the prices of NAC gas.
turns.zh: 嗯，其实我在某种意义上认为两者都对：交易者的布局确实符合基本面。有强劲的产量、库存累积、天气导致的电力需求下降，所有这些因素都会压低天然气（nat gas）的价格。

turns.en: And traders clearly have been positioning for this. And this has now built a clear extreme. We're pretty much now at the zero percentile on every major look back.
turns.zh: 交易者显然一直在为此布局。而这现在已经形成了一个明显的极端。我们几乎在每一个主要回看周期上都处于零百分位。

turns.en: This is now extreme gross and net short positioning in here. This is a very crowded trade, but no trigger has yet emerged that would potentially play a, the catalyst in causing a short squeeze.
turns.zh: 如今这里是极端的总空头和净空头持仓。这是一个非常拥挤的交易，但还没有出现任何可能充当催化剂、引发空头挤压的触发因素。

turns.en: But the fuel is there. And this is where I would be very careful. I think this is a perfect example that if you want to stay short, natural gas, you need to put that on with some sort of convexity or overlay some sort of an options hedge, because in the past, when natural guests gets this kind of positioning, it can cause some very serious volatility when a squeeze occurs.
turns.zh: 但“燃料”已经在那里了。这正是我会非常小心的地方。我觉得这是一个完美的例子：如果你想继续做空天然气，你就需要给它配上某种凸性，或者叠加某种期权对冲，因为在过去，当天然气出现这种持仓时，一旦发生挤压，就可能引发非常严重的波动。

turns.en: And so this is a perfect example of when carrying some sort of hedges on any short positioning makes the most sense. And for any listeners, I want to dig into these positioning charts.
turns.zh: 所以这是一个完美的例子，说明在任何空头持仓上带某种对冲是最有意义的。而对于任何想深入研究这些持仓图表的听众……

turns.zh: 你可以在 cotsignal.com（拼作 C-O-T-S-I-G-N-A-L.com）免费找到全部内容。——简单提醒一句，Maseel：我想提醒听众，持仓报告并不是水晶球。

turns.zh: 它是一张“拥挤度地图”，显示交易者在哪里已经重仓、并可能因此脆弱。但这并不总是意味着反转迫在眉睫。

turns.en: It's just an indication of an incredibly crowded positioning. All right. Thank you, Patrick. And that's it for this week's episode. Thank you so much.
